description.narrative:
The goal is: To increase the safety of NGO staff members, program beneficiaries and improve the overall impact, accountability and effectiveness of NGO programming and their partners in Uganda.
The specific objective is: To strengthen the capacity of NGOs and their partners to establish effective organizational systems, policies, and improve knowledge to control internal risks, sexual exploitation, harassment and all forms of abuse or breaches by NGO staff and their partners.
Outcome 1: Improve organisational culture, value and ethics regarding internal risk management of NGOs and their partners by establishing effective internal control mechanisms including predictive controls, preventative controls, detective controls, monitoring controls and responding to controls breaches based on the recommendations from phase two.
Output 1.1: 40 NGO leaders (directors, board members and senior leadership team) trained on Creating and Maintaining a Sustainable Ethical Culture in Internal Risk Management Output 1.2: 50 Member Organisations that participated in phase two risk management training and have implemented their action plans Output 1.3: 30 NGO organisations that have received technical support in Internal Risk Management.
Outcome 2: Improve the safeguarding practices of NGOs and their partners to reduce the risks of sexual exploitation, harassment and all forms of abuse in NGO programming in Uganda based on the recommendations from phase two.
Output 2.1: 40 NGO leaders (directors, board members, and senior leadership team) trained on governance in safeguarding (Establishing a Safe Culture - Tone at the Top) Output 2.2: NGO focal persons trained as Trainers of Trainers Output 2.3: IRMG member organisations have adopted standardised safeguarding policies, tools and guidelines Output 2.4: IRMG member organisations have carried out safeguarding risk assessment and management process.
Outcome 3: Leverage lessons learned and knowledge of the IRMG to benefit the wider civil society sector in Uganda to improve on managing wrongful conduct, including safeguarding practices and the prevention of Internal Risks through the IRMG Steering Committee, Communities of Practices (CoP) and the Online Resource Hub.
Output 3.1: IRMG Steering Committee and Project Management Team meets to provide technical guidance and support to the IRMG programming Output 3.2: Continuation and sustainability of the established Community of Practices (CoP) Initiatives Output 3.3: Engagement of members and the wider NGO sector using the online resource hub Output 3.4: Review of commitment of current members and on-boarding at least 10 more National NGOs
Outcome 4: Improve the capacity of NGOs and their partners to implement safe, confidential and effective complaints handling, reporting and feedback, case management and investigations mechanisms based on the recommendations from phase two.
Output 4.1: Member Organisations are trained on setting up effective internal risk management mechanisms, controls and investigations Output 4.2: Member Organisations are trained on setting up effective safeguarding case management and investigations mechanisms

The “Internal Risk Management Group” (IRMG) in Uganda, which currently consists of 69 international and national non-governmental organizations (Non Government Organizations), is applying through “Plan International Uganda” as a agreement partner, for funding of SEK 6 million to implement Phase 3 of the "Internal Risk Management Group (IRMG), Uganda" program for a period of 36 months with a preliminary start date of 1 July 2022.
The initiative aims to influence and improve accountability and efficiency in INGO and NGO members' programs by:
1) Strengthen organizational culture with the aim of preventing and counteracting fraud and corruption.
2) Strengthen the protection mechanisms and processes of INGO and NGO members and manage risks of sexual harassment, exploitation and abuse.
3) Draw on the lessons and knowledge of IRMG members in favor of the civil society sector in Uganda to improve the management of irregularities, including all forms of violations, and to combat fraud and corruption.
Plan International Uganda and IRMG will implement the intervention together with local civil society organizations in Uganda.
The contribution's total budget is SEK 6 million, most of which will be used by Plan International Uganda, where the intervention will be implemented. The agreement partner will be Plan International Uganda.

“Internal Risk Management Group” (IRMG) i Uganda, som för närvarande består av 69 internationella icke-statliga organisationer (Non Government Organisations), söker genom och ”Plan International Uganda” som avtalspartner, om finansiering om 6 miljoner SEK för att implementera Fas 3 av programmet "Internal Risk Management Group (IRMG), Uganda" under en period om 36 månader med preliminärt startdatum 1 juli 2022.
Insatsen syftar till att påverka och förbättra ansvarsutkrävande och effektivitet i INGO och NGO medlemmars program genom att:
1) Stärka organisationskultur med syfte att förebygga och motverka bedrägeri och korruption.
2) Stärka skyddsmekanismer och processer hos INGO och NGO medlemmar och hantera risker för sexuella trakasserier, utnyttjande och missbruk.
3) Dra på lärdomar och kunskap från IRMG medlemmar till fördel för civilsamhällssektorn i Uganda för att förbättra hantering av oegentligheter, inklusive alla former av kränkningar samt för att motverka bedrägeri och korruption.
Plan International Uganda och IRMG kommer att implementera insatsen tillsammans med lokala civilsamhällsorganisationer i Uganda.
Insatsens totala budget är 6 miljoner SEK varav merparten kommer att användas av Plan International Uganda där insatsen implementeras. Avtalspart blir Plan International Uganda.

title.narrative: Decision Internal Risk Management Group (IRMG) project

description.narrative:
The most recent narrative report shows that, during the second year of Phase 3 (January-December 2024), the Internal Risk Management Group (IRMG) focused on completing follow-up investigation trainings and providing post-training technical support to its members.
The report is structured into the following sections: (i) Follow-up on investigation trainings (ii) Internal funding (iii) External funding (iv) External engagements (v) Communication and visibility (vi) Programme auditing (vii) Programme financial reporting
Key achievements and areas of focus during the period include:
https://trac.sida.se/api/answerimage/8766?fileName=691dded8f87f428fb97aa29b6d5b8438.png
Sida assesses that IRMG has achieved significant progress despite being a relatively small programme. Programme Manager Henry Owara plays a crucial role, effectively managing most of the programme independently with support from its members. Henry Owara has worked diligently to transition IRMG into an autonomous organisation, as its current status under Plan International has made it challenging to attract support from other development partners and institutions. Sweden is proud that IRMG is now nearing full independence, which aligns well with Sida's objective of supporting initiatives that become self-sustaining in the long term.
With an increase in demand for competent risk management and safeguarding officers as well as the recent transition from Human Resources (HR) Offices to People and Culture, the responsibility was on Internal Risk Management Group (IRMG) to respond to the ever-changing capacity needs of its members. The main achievements by the time of reporting (December 2023);
Six comprehensive trainings has been successfully completed in phase 3, year 1:
• 3-day per session per location country-wide risk management training in 8 locations for focal persons, • 1-day risk management training for directors and the senior leadership teams, • 3-day per session per location country-wide safeguarding training in 8 locations for focal persons, • 1-day safeguarding training for directors and the senior leadership teams, • 5-day risk management investigations training and • 5-day safeguarding case management and investigations training.
The IRMG project team has also broadened their engagements with other key stakeholders and established additional strategic alliances. The project has managed to engage the U4 AntiCorruption Resource Centre, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), the Safeguarding Resource Hub, the UN Office of the Resident Coordinator (Uganda), SOTERIA/Interpol and Charter for Change (C4C).
IRMG still face challenges with finding new donors and acquiring additional funding apart from Sida. One initiative has been to establish an annual subscription fees for all the 72 members organizations. However, in year 1 only 10 out of the 55 active members have paid their annual subscriptions for 2023.
Based on IRMGs advocacy strategy, initially aiming at popularizing their activities and presence in the NGO sector, more interest had been put on implementing the strategy through workshops and visibility notices. In phase 3, thus, the focus had been put on ensuring that the online hub was fully utilized.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
